technical_and_design_decisions: Build on the Spring XD module model (Java 17 / Spring Framework 6 baseline): implement Kafka source and sink, generator source, and perf-meter sink as deployable XD modules with declarative options metadata.

Kafka source uses the low-level (simple) consumer API to provide deterministic partition assignment and explicit offset control; offsets are tracked externally (ZooKeeper/Kafka offset storage) with handling for broker leader changes and reconnects.
Kafka sink uses the Kafka producer API with configurable encoder/serializer, partitioning strategy, and acknowledgment mode.
Generator source emits synthetic byte-array messages with configurable options numMsgs (default 10000), msgSize (default 1024), and numThreads (default 1), using a thread-safe atomic counter.
Perf-meter sink logs timestamp, cumulative message count, and message rate (messages/second since last log event) to the container log via SLF4J every numMsgs messages (default 1000).

Custom-module installation is exposed as a REST endpoint accepting a multipart uber-jar upload; the server validates the archive, registers it in the module repository/registry, propagates it to containers, and a corresponding xd-shell command is added for the client side.
Test strategy: unit tests with mocks plus integration tests against an embedded Kafka broker, wired into the existing CI build.
Sample reference app is delivered as a standalone GitHub repository with provisioning scripts (e.g., Docker/Vagrant) demonstrating Kafka as message bus and as source.
assumptions: A single experienced developer (familiar with Spring, Spring Integration, Spring XD internals, and Kafka) performs all work; estimates are focused-effort workdays (8 hours), not elapsed time.

A working development environment with the Spring XD codebase, build system, and access to a Kafka broker for development and testing is available or quickly provisioned; an embedded Kafka broker is usable in automated tests.

U1 is a broad epic/vision statement; this increment delivers the Kafka-based ingestion path plus performance tooling as concrete steps toward it. Actual HDFS/HAWQ/GPDB target loaders are out of scope for this increment beyond high-level architecture notes.
U2 is a spike only: research and documentation, no production code; its output feeds the Kafka source implementation.
U3 scope covers server-side REST endpoint, module registry/repository integration, propagation to containers, and a shell command; no web UI is required.
U7 is a measurement/analysis activity using the singlenode container, not a new code deliverable.
Peer/code review effort is included in the final integration activity; documentation targets are READMEs and the project wiki.

activities.activity_description: Set up the development environment (Spring XD build, Kafka broker for dev/test, singlenode container), define module architecture consistent with the XD module model, and outline how the increment supports the mass-ingestion goal of U1.

activities.activity_name: U2 spike: study Kafka simple consumer API
activities.activity_description: Study the Kafka simple (low-level) consumer API covering partition metadata lookup, offset management, leader handling, and fetch requests; build a small throwaway prototype; document findings, recommended approach, and next steps.

activities.activity_name: Kafka source module implementation (simple consumer API)
activities.activity_description: Implement the Kafka source module based on spike findings: deterministic partition assignment, explicit offset control and persistence, broker/leader failure handling, reconnect logic, configuration options, and basic verification.
Implement the Kafka sink module using the producer API with configurable encoder/serializer, partitioning, and acknowledgment settings, plus basic verification.

activities.activity_name: U3: REST API for custom module (uber-jar) upload and installation
activities.activity_description: Design and implement the REST endpoint for uploading a custom module packaged as an uber-jar, including archive validation, registration in the module repository/registry, propagation to cluster containers, a matching xd-shell command, and API-level tests.

activities.activity_name: U4: sample GitHub reference app for XD cluster with Kafka
activities.activity_description: Create a standalone GitHub sample project with provisioning scripts demonstrating Spring XD with Kafka as message bus and Kafka as source, including stream definitions and README documentation.

Implement the generator source module producing a configurable number of messages of a specified size across configurable threads (numMsgs/msgSize/numThreads with defaults 10000/1024/1), including unit tests.
Implement the perf-meter sink that logs timestamp, message count, and message rate since the last log event every numMsgs messages (default 1000) to the container log, including unit tests.

activities.activity_name: U7: performance measurement with generator | perf-meter on singlenode
activities.activity_description: Deploy and run the generator | perf-meter stream on XD's singlenode container ingesting 1M messages of 1000 bytes with one thread, collect throughput/latency characteristics, perform light tuning, and document results.

activities.activity_name: U8: automated test coverage for Kafka source and sink modules
activities.activity_description: Write unit and integration tests (using an embedded Kafka broker) covering Kafka source and sink functionality, failure/reconnect scenarios, and wire the tests into the CI build.

activities.activity_name: Integration, code review, documentation and release readiness
activities.activity_description: Integrate all modules, run end-to-end verification, incorporate review feedback, finalize documentation (READMEs/wiki), and prepare the increment for release.
